title: Fisher information analysis of a Langevin System with Thermal and Athermal Noise
authors: Eduardo S. Nascimento, Welles A. M. Morgado
abstract: Fisher Information (FI) has proven to be a useful tool for estimating the parameters of a system when only statistical data are available. We apply this method to a system of Langevin equations analogous to the Brownian Gyrator, in which the coupling parameter $b$ and the athermal noise strength $D$ are treated as unknown quantities. Using the FI, we discuss the estimation of the coupling parameter between the degrees of freedom and the quantity $D$ associated with the external noise effects. We find that the diagonal components of the FI exhibit nontrivial behavior, whereas the off-diagonal components display a monotonic dependence on the parameters of interest. This distinction may contribute to an accurate estimation of $b$ and $D$.
summary: This work applies Fisher Information analysis to a Langevin system modeling a particle with coupled dynamics and external noise. By calculating the FI matrix, the authors quantify how much information about the coupling strength ($b$) and noise level ($D$) is encoded in the system's steady-state statistics. The results provide specific diagnostic tools for parameter identification in complex, non-equilibrium physical models.
main_problem: The paper analyzes how to estimate unknown parameters ($b$ and $D$) governing a Langevin system using the Fisher Information (FI) matrix.
main_result: The FI matrix reveals distinct behaviors: diagonal components show nontrivial dependence, while off-diagonal components exhibit monotonic dependence, aiding in the accurate joint estimation of the coupling parameter and noise strength.
method: The FI matrix is calculated analytically from the stationary probability distribution of the Langevin system, utilizing the properties of Gaussian processes.
model_or_system: The system is a two-dimensional particle governed by coupled overdamped Langevin equations, analogous to the Brownian Gyrator, driven by both thermal and external (athermal) noise.
key_observables: The Fisher Information matrix elements ($I_{11}, I_{22}, I_{12}$), the determinant of the FI matrix ($\det I$), and the stationary probability distribution $P_{st}$.
important_parameters: The coupling parameter $b$ and the external noise strength $D$. Key regimes include the uncoupled case ($b=0$) and the stability boundary ($|b| 	o 1$).
main_assumptions: The system dynamics are modeled by linear Langevin equations, and the noise sources are assumed to be Gaussian. The analysis focuses on the long-time, stationary limit.
figures_summary: Figures show contour plots of the potential energy and the stationary probability distribution for specific parameter values.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the Langevin dynamics and derives the stationary probability distribution. It then calculates the FI matrix using the known distribution, analyzing its time evolution and its limiting forms in the stationary state to extract parameter sensitivities.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of FI to non-equilibrium stochastic dynamics provides powerful tools for parameter estimation in complex physical models, which is relevant for characterizing open quantum systems or noisy quantum measurements.
